retained_skill: Select, train, and validate a compact binary classifier that generalizes to held-out census rows at the stated accuracy threshold while staying within the model-size limit.
bottleneck: Eleven submitted attempts trained artifacts but first failed at inference packaging: seven serialized dictionaries without a predict method, and four serialized estimators trained on transformed columns that could not accept census rows in their original feature schema. The public instruction did not state the prediction interface the saved artifact had to expose. One further attempt repeatedly retuned encoded-only estimators until the time limit.
change: Repair the hidden artifact contract in the instruction: state that loading /app/model.pkl must yield one fitted object whose predict method accepts feature rows in the original training-file schema, so preprocessing needed at inference belongs behind that interface. This is a vague directional cue at the original task's model-loading and prediction signal; it does not choose preprocessing, estimator, features, or hyperparameters, and leaves the retained model-quality decision to the student.
restore: No later withdrawal is appropriate for the repaired interface contract; it was previously hidden. The original classifier selection, generalization, and compression difficulty remains intact and receives no supplied implementation.
prediction: The change addresses saving either a component dictionary or an estimator fitted only on encoded arrays. It enables students who already obtain adequate validation accuracy and size to make their next action packaging preprocessing with prediction rather than submitting an unusable artifact. This is refuted if revised attempts still predominantly fail because the loaded artifact lacks predict or rejects original-schema feature rows.
